_note: The legacy automatic gate collection remains retired. What is permitted is the continuity plane below and nothing else: SessionStart restores the canonical project checkpoint; UserPromptSubmit runs the single unprompted-speech chokepoint; Stop may nudge one explicitly authorized project-scoped objective AND capture a project snapshot; PreCompact and SessionEnd capture a project snapshot. Version 3 of this file permitted exactly two handlers, which was not a safety property but a contradiction: it demanded a restore while forbidding any event that could WRITE the journal the restore reads, so the canonical store held zero progression rows. Adding to this list is still a deliberate act that must pass `npm run hooks:check`; what changed is that the shape can now express the plane that actually works.

_eventOwners.responsibility: Restore the newest coherent committed checkpoint. Reads only; ADR-073 §5 forbids replaying the outbox here because replay is a write and a write costs more than this boundary's whole budget.
The sole writer of unprompted user-facing bytes (ADR-040 / DDD-0004). Producers run as candidates behind it; it alone applies policy and writes the envelope.
May request one continuation for one explicitly authorized, project-scoped objective read from the user's own work ledger (ADR-043). Never a refusal, never a second task store.
Append one project snapshot to the canonical store and commit any outbox debt a previously interrupted session left behind.
The boundary at which context is about to be lost — capture before it is.
The boundary at which the session is about to be gone — capture before it is.

_notInThisPlane.reachability: Registered in hook-shim.mjs's dispatch table as a blocking PreToolUse route and reachable by explicit invocation. It composes every policy that could refuse one Write into ONE decision with declared precedence and one reason. It is absent from the continuity plane because refusal authorization is not lifecycle continuity — not because it was retired.

Reachable through `npm run execution-policy:check` and scripts/execution-policy.mjs at the host's consequential-execution boundary. It is an authorization decision point, not an automatic lifecycle registration.

_codexCapture.method: A probe hook was registered in a temporary CODEX_HOME on all twelve event names the installed binary declares, and a real `codex exec "reply OK"` was run against it.

notObserved.Stop: The probe turn never completed, so run_turn_stop_hooks had no completion to fire on. The binary declares the event and StopCommandOutputWire, so this is not-proven rather than unsupported. Stop keeps only the pre-existing continuation gate; no capture handler was added to an event whose delivery has not been seen.
notObserved.PreCompact: A one-line turn never approaches a compaction threshold. The binary declares PreCompact and PreCompactCommandOutputWire. No capture handler registered.

_codexCapture.consequence: Codex captures at SessionEnd only. Cross-host resume is therefore Claude-captured -> Codex-restored and Codex-captured (SessionEnd) -> Claude-restored; it must not be described as symmetrical across every boundary.

matcherAllowlist.reason: SessionStart is a lifecycle source matcher, not a tool matcher.
UserPromptSubmit is a prompt lifecycle event, not a tool matcher; the runtime is the sole writer of unprompted bytes (ADR-040/DDD-0004).
Stop is a lifecycle event; wildcard is the host contract.
PreCompact is a lifecycle event; wildcard is the host contract.
SessionEnd is a lifecycle event; wildcard is the host contract.
